name: LYONDELL CHEMICAL CHANNELVIEW

reports_to_state.source: TCEQ Air Emission Event Report Database (STEERS), cached detail pages

reports.cause_excerpt: A suction pressure transmitter on the vent gas compressor froze, which shut down the compressor, causing the vent gas header to pressure up. The increased header pressure caused PVRV's on two tanks…
A process upset caused the POTBA unit to shut down, resulting in venting to the flare system. In addition, the emergency flare EFL86902 smoked for approximately 29 minutes.
Power outage resulting in flaring from multiple flares.
Process unit upset caused excessive flaring exceeding RQ at POSM1 Emergency Flare and opacity at POSM1 Emergency and Continuous Flares
Pressure inside tank TK-81370 increased, causing the tank relief device to open to atmosphere.
Crack developed on weld under insulation releasing process vapor to the atmosphere in excess of the reportable quantity.

reports_to_epa.source: EPA Toxics Release Inventory via Envirofacts
reports_to_epa.note: Pounds per year, stack plus fugitive air releases; a null means the form gave no number.

caveats: Being upwind of a spike is not evidence of anything; wind at one monitor cannot tell facilities apart.
Reports listed here are what the facility reported to the state (TCEQ STEERS); amounts are the facility's own estimates.
TRI figures are what the facility reports to EPA each year for routine releases; they are estimates, not measurements, and not events.
